newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto group to buy Astra stake at market prices.
newsitem.headline: Suharto group to buy Astra stake at market prices.

text.p: A group to which Indonesia's President Suharto is linked has said it will not make a general offer for shares in Astra International, but will buy stock at market prices, Bisnis Indonesia reported on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted Nusamba group commisioner timber baron Muhamad "Bob" Hasan as saying in an interview that the venture will not buy into Astra, the country's largest vehicle manufacturer, if the share price is too high.
Hasan said Nusamba was willing to consider offers from existing shareholders but would not make a tender offer itself.
He declined to say if any shareholders had offered to sell their holdings. "It is my company secret. I cannot let you know," he said.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto, and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.

Astra shares soared last month on newspaper reports that a takeover bid may be in progress but tapered off after tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna announced he had bought a 9.81 percent stake in the firm.
His PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna cigarette company then announced that a subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent stake in Astra, giving Putera Sampoerna effectively the largest shareholding.
Newspapers at the time said Sampoerna might sell his stake to Nusamba, which Hasan denied.
Astra is a widely-held company and brokers have said an 18-20 percent stake may be sufficient to gain a controlling interest.
Japan's Toyota Motor Co holds an 8.26 percent stake.
